ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the upper vertex, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; D is located on side AB, E is located on side AC, segment DE connects D and E, and from the figure and the meaning of the problem it can be known that DE is parallel to the base BC. Reasoning: Because DE parallel BC, triangle ADE and triangle ABC are similar by AA. Corresponding sides are proportional: AD/AB = AE/AC. Substitute AD = 2, AB = 6, AE = 3, obtaining 2/6 = 3/AC. Cross-multiplying gives 2AC = 18, therefore AC = 9.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A is the top vertex of triangle ABC, D lies on side AB, E lies on side AC, and the segment DE is drawn parallel to the base BC. From the text, use AD = 2, AB = 6, AE = 3, and the target is AC. Since DE is parallel to BC, triangles ADE and ABC are similar by AA similarity. Set the corresponding-side ratio AD/AB = AE/AC, so 2/6 = 3/AC. Solve to get AC = 9.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: D divides side AB and E divides side AC, with DE parallel to BC. From the text, AD = 2 and AB = 6, so DB = AB - AD = 4; also AE = 3. Apply the basic proportionality theorem to the two sides cut by the parallel line: AD/DB = AE/EC. Substitute 2/4 = 3/EC, giving EC = 6. Then AC = AE + EC = 3 + 6 = 9.
